questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures, the mountains, Academic opportunities, career opportunities, traveling

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Best university in the EU for my studies (when not counting UK)

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy, all information was provided prior to arrival or during my first days here.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Mails and meetings regarding the housing, very nice informative student association helped out a lot

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very easy, WOKO basically found one to you through ETH zurich

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's nice because then you have a life outside campus ;-)

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Nice to live so many people together, not nice during corona, nice to being forced to make new friends when you live 170 exchange students together.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: They guide you all the way regarding how to upload documents and how to apply for specific courses. really helpful administration

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: See above

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I registered for 6, got all of them except one of them - and then applied for another one and got that one

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be on time. It becomes messy when u have to fill out docs after deadlines.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The students here are less curious - thats why its not a 5

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: They were similar to the level of UCPH I'd say

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I only took practical courses and project works, so I didn't really experience the lecture and theoretical exercise classes. However, the practical work was really good - a bit too pedagogical sometimes..

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Intensive german language course, cell biology of the nucleus, membrane biology, insulin signaling, RNA biology, genomic and genetic methods in cell and developmental biology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I'd recommend all of them actually. The language course gives you a lot of new friends that are also on an exchange. All of the others were lab-based lab courses where you are assigned to a Ph.D. or post-doc project and work on those projects for around a month. Insulin Signaling is quite intense in terms of the lab work. But the nice thing is that you try out a lot of different techniques.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I traveled a lot on the weekends and the personal spending per month listed is mainly due to the high cost of public transport traveling within Switzerland..

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing was less, food and especially transportation were more

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: All sports you can imagine were for free during ASVZ and I am super amazed by all the different sports you could try out during the time at ETH Zurich. Something I was really happy about!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: My student association arranged a lot of different social get-together events (dinner evenings, board game evenings etc..) and also on Campus quite some academic activities were planned. ESN network also arranges some nice activities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: ASVZ for sports! Dinner evenings etc with your student association! If you want to go on a trip with other exchange students and don't have a group to go with, go on an ESN trip!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I love mountains (mountaineering like hiking, climbing, via ferrata, skiing etc) and Switzerland is ideal for this! I went every weekend and I already miss the mountains

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, it is quite similar to Danish culture on the surface, however, some swiss people can be a bit "shy" or ignorant maybe. But when you get to know the, they typically become your new best friends ;-)

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: ASVZ! ESN! Student associations! Language courses! Parties at exchange dorm rooms and at "Langstrasse"! Get a buddy (a local student to help you out with socializing and meeting new people on bars etc)!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The language barrier sometimes. Swiss german is nothing like high german - however, most people here speak English

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The very active culture in terms of sports and the high degree of citizens being international

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: ASVZ for sports (try everything out, jazz dance, ballet, kickboxing, swimming, judo whatever), do travel while being here if you like the alps, engage in academic activities outside your syllabus if you have time (they normally organize cool lecture-based and coffee events where you can learn about anything you like with fellow students of yours!)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Apply for Novo Nordisk Intwrnational Talent program as this will give you money for traveling ;-) I don't regret a sec that I used all of the money on traveling even though sometimes I couldn't afford high-quality meals on every hike I went on;-)

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the traveling and cultural experiences learned. ANd then also the nice network you get if you are a biology student and choose block courses (YOU SHOULD DO THIS!!!!!!) because you will get to know a lot of lab members within the different labs. This enables you to explore different fields of biology and let you to find out what you fancy more than other subjects :DD

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Money for all the traveling :O

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer:
DO reach out if you want to hear more about the experiences here, I'd be happy to help out with more details :) -  I think it is super important to go on an exchange if you have eager to learn about other cultures and foreign ways of teaching etc

OMG and the mountains!!! ;-)))

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
